hero.subtitle: Helping college students navigate housing with AI

blocks.text: Find your next place at Cornell, *described in your own words*.

CUApts is a Cornell DTI project that helps students find off-campus housing by browsing listings and reading real reviews from other Cornellians. 

I designed its AI / LLM search bar. Users describe what they're looking for in their own words, and CUApts builds an informed answer around their request: deciding whether they'll find top picks, a budget comparison, or a neighborhood guide most relevant.

blocks.alt: AI search results for 4-person rentals close to West Campus

blocks.text: Problem: the housing search is overwhelming
College students who are looking for an apartment for the first time have endless options and factors to weigh, and navigating complex filters or searching apartment by address only makes it harder.

blocks.label: Objective
blocks.text: How might we give users a way to easily navigate *complex preferences* and find apartments that meet their constraints?
Because LLM search is a relatively new field without concrete UI/UX rules, I researched how current AI products help users navigate the novel technology and how they structure their responses.

lines.text: One open field that lets users ask in plain language instead of using filters.
Example prompts under the input to help users understand how best to use the tool.
Search modes switch inside the same input so users never leave the page.

items.text: Division into sections for improved readability rather than one long, unbroken response
A glowing design motif to indicate the use of AI

blocks.text: How should *AI search* differ from normal search?

cons.text: Doesn't explain reasoning behind the results

pros.text: Shows listings in the context of the user's constraints
Combination of text and components makes scanning easy while still providing reasoning

items.title: Problem
items.body: Students search with a set of constraints (roommates, distance to campus, budget), but a list of results doesn't show which ones each apartment meets.

items.title: Solution
items.body: Instead of auto-applying filters, the LLM builds each answer from a library of components, picking the ones that best explain the results, so it's clear how each apartment fits what the user asked for.

lines.text: *Which places match?* Top picks, using the same cards users already see when browsing.
*How do they compare?* Price + key features shown side by side. Each row expands to show the listing and a relevant review.
*Where should I live?* A breakdown of each neighborhood, with a link to narrow the search.

blocks.label: Built to Scale
blocks.text: New CUApts features can easily be added to the set of components the AI uses to build its answers, making the feature scalable as the platform grows.

items.title: Exploring an *emergent* field in design
items.body: UX for AI/LLM is a relatively new space without as many set conventions. I enjoyed learning about the patterns that are starting to emerge through market research and how to incorporate innovation in a way that's easy for users to understand.

items.title: Designing with *developers*
items.body: Handoff involved documenting the component system and user flow in detail to ensure they understood my vision for the feature. Working closely with developers to balance design with feasibility, I gained a better understanding of how design and programming come together in a product environment.
